pitch_detail.notes: Easy ramp terrain to a belay at the foot of a left-facing corner.
Jam the corner crack until it widens and a roof blocks it, then go left and layback a thin flake to a good stance and belay.
Easier but loose rock, scrambled, leads to a solid ledge under a squeeze chimney.
Enter the chimney just left of the golden block for a body length or two, then keep going left on good climbing to a roomy ledge below a golden face.
Starting at the ledge's left end, link several cracks over a small roof.
Go left around a corner and up a crumbly ramp, then stem and use paired cracks to reach a spacious bivy ledge.
A splitter crack rising straight from the ledge up the golden wall, aiming for a small chimney and a roof.
Take the right-facing corner rising from the ledge, through a second roof to a small ledge, then angle left up a very thin seam for an airy finish.
Walk up and right on easy third class to a corner system left of the obvious gully, and stem and jam it until the terrain eases to third class. A walk leads from here to the summit.

review.changed: Wrote all nine pitches with grades and lengths. Third pitch given as easy fifth class.

pitch_detail.notes: Easy mixed terrain, entered by a traverse from the right, gives access to the ice. The first steep curtain may be thin and hollow. After the traverse the ice can be candled, and solid placements might require digging through poor ice and snow.
Climb a steep corner of candled, possibly rotten ice, using the rock of the left wall for stemming. Belay at the base of a snowfield.
Snow and ice, about WI3 in feel, up to the Black Dike and Teepe Col.

review.changed: Wrote three pitches as described for one ascent in early season conditions. No lengths or bolt counts.
review.other_findings: Conditions in the account were thin, hollow, rotten ice; the third pitch is only 'WI3ish'.

pitch_detail.notes: Vertical climbing to a high first bolt, then to a cave belay. Consider pre-clipping if descending by rappel and unsure of the style.

Angle up and right from the cave on sustained ground to a wild, difficult leftward traverse. Long slings help at the start of the traverse. At the hanging belay, the second can slip below it and take the next lead, which keeps the ropes tidy.
Traverse left a few more metres, then steep climbing through two boulder-problem sections to another comfortable cave belay.
Vertical slab, then a hard bouldery sequence over a gentle bulge, and a traverse left to a belay on slab.
A very long sustained slab up the headwall, with a short traverse to a small cave belay.
Mild edging to a large ledge with trees.
The last stretch to the summit, with bolts spaced fairly far apart.

review.changed: Wrote all seven pitches with grades and lengths. No rappel table: only that the top four stations carry cord with rings.

pitch_detail.notes: Straightforward ice about 30 m long. A number of minor bulges and steps lie in the stretch before the second pitch.
A short, very easy pitch up into the bowl where the final pitch lies.
Steep ice out of a rock amphitheater, the hardest pitch. Above it, only short lower-angle steps.

review.changed: Wrote three pitches; the first pitch length is approximate so is kept in notes.

pitch_detail.notes: Starts by the river after a rappel in through the slot. Ice climbing to the base of the short second pitch.
A short, possibly insecure step; consider leaving a fixed rope here. A trail crosses the route above.
Ice above the trail crossing. Rappel from trees.
Steeper ice. Rappel from trees.
The tube, the hardest pitch. A walk-off is possible on skier's left after this pitch.
A rolling sheet of ice about a 5-10 minute hike above pitch 5.

review.changed: Wrote all six pitches with grades and lengths. No rappel table: only that pitches 3 and 4 are rappelled from trees.
review.other_findings: Stored 5 pitches; the account lists six (a trail crosses between P2 and P3, and P6 is a hike above P5).

pitch_detail.notes: Steep face on a black streak; belay on the right. Quickdraws.
Tricky face moves to a left-facing corner crack, then a tricky topout onto a small grassy ledge. Draws and a single rack. Can be linked from P1; consider hauling the rack to the mid anchor.

Clip high, move firmly left over a slabby ramp, then head up and left to a wide sloping ledge, with the belay set off to the left near your feet. Protect the follower on arriving at the ledge. This pitch and the two below can be skipped by scrambling up from the talus cone.
Go directly up a steep bulge using sidepulls to a stance, traverse left over a 5.10- slab, and rejoin the arete above.

The long White Crack pitch. Step left into a left-facing corner, then follow the crack through a juggy white dike. Shallow corner layback crux low, another where it seams out. Not sustained, with rests, but long. Save a piece or two for the top. Belay well up and left. Optional stances around mid-height, or a fixed belay at about 37 m.

review.changed: Wrote all five pitches with grades and lengths. No rappel table: descent is a set of rope-length options, not a fixed list.

pitch_detail.notes: After a steep snow approach, climb the ice smear of about 20 m up and to the right and belay where the ice runs out. The ice is solid and takes screws well.
Plod up snow for the remainder of the couloir. Slide hazard is a real concern, and there is little to place for protection.

review.changed: Wrote both pitches. The ice smear is about 20 m, kept in notes. No grades given per pitch.

pitch_detail.notes: Look for the offwidth along the west side of the arch on the south face. Step onto a little ledge beside it, then combine jamming and stemming inside the arch. Chimneys continue to a broad ledge; keep burrowing up and right through caves to a big sloping shelf, enclosed by walls and capped by a roof, where you belay.

Climb or aid to the horizontal crack below a nearly horizontal 15-foot roof, then tension-traverse out to place your biggest cam (at least a #4). Aid out the narrowing crack in the roof; a fixed ball nut sits at the corner. A few tenuous placements with some deck potential lead around the roof corner to the belay. May go free at a hard 5.something.

review.changed: Wrote both pitches. No lengths given.

pitch_detail.notes: Slabs take you to a chimney, followed by simple grassy ground and a second chimney to top out.
The crux is a leaning corner with a fist-size crack running down its middle. Next, a further corner crack gives a second layback section, and one more crack in a corner finishes it.
Climb right through a stack of granite slices, following the best crack to a grassy dihedral. About 20 m more reaches the summit.

review.changed: Wrote all three pitches. The 20 m to the summit is described in the last pitch notes.

pitch_detail.notes: Climb loose, grassy slab left of a big yellow roof. Station at a flake below a vertical dihedral.
A steep corner holding some loose flakes is the crux. Beyond comes a ledge; shift left to the next corner, with sound rock, small edges and fun moves, ending on a good grassy ledge.
Enjoyable climbing on solid rock up a corner, with a hard final move as you cross leftward. The anchor is on a moss-covered pad.
Take the clear dihedral overhead, keeping left for the first few metres. After a small corner, the anchor sits on a mossy pad off to the left.
Another obvious dihedral to the right, with a short layback section and poor protection to reach the main shoulder. Anchor 8 m left of the ridge.

review.changed: Wrote all five pitches with grades and lengths. No rappel table: descent is 'rap the route' with no station list.

pitch_detail.notes: A short step up onto a large ledge.
The ridge proper begins here. Go up about 40 to 50 m to a good belay stance.
Relaxed, well-protected ridge climbing up to the overhang visible from the base. Belay on top of the block.
Belay standing on the large block (poorly protected; pins or a bolt kit may help). Step out onto the east face to a crack system and follow it to the summit.

review.changed: Wrote the four pitches. Pitch 2 length is a range (40-50 m) so kept in notes. No grades by pitch.
review.other_findings: Reported rockfall since the route was first climbed.

pitch_detail.notes: Depending on conditions this can be a detached ice pillar, a snow pillar or just rock. It gives onto a ramp that runs to the start of the WI3 pitch.
In good condition, a pleasant ice pitch of about 18 m; the form varies.
Leads up a chimney, which may hold ice. Carry rock gear, pins included, in case it does not. Ends on a ledge, above which easy climbing reaches the ridge top.

review.changed: Wrote three pitches; condition-dependent forms noted. Easy terrain above the chimney not written.
review.other_findings: Pitch 2 ice length (18 m) applies when in good condition.

pitch_detail.notes: The one pitch protected entirely by bolts. Slippery heather leads up to the slab; clip a low bolt, shift left to a grubby ledge, then smear to bolt two. The hardest move of the route comes next: smeary feet and just a tiny edge for both hands. Easy slab climbing finishes over the lip to the anchor.

Follow the bolt line up the slanting ramp left of the anchor to a small vertical lip. Pulling the lip on smeary feet is the pitch's hard bit, then an easy crack to the anchor. Small cams for the end if you want to protect it.

Follow a shallow corner until it turns to slab, then bolts up and right to a thin crack or seam, where a shallow .3 cam backed up by a .2 fits. A smeary hard move leads to a bolt and easy ground to the anchor. Easy to link into the next pitch.

Slab so gentle it is nearly a walk leads to a bolt, then toward mossy ledges where a second bolt is clipped before pulling to a ledge under a large roof. Only two bolts and very easy. Link it with P3, or skip it when descending by rappel.

review.changed: Wrote all four pitches with grades and lengths. No rappel table: rappelling follows the climbed pitches, not a listed station order.

pitch_detail.notes: Fingers for a long way, then a stemming box move just before the second roof, to a gear belay on a sloping ledge.
Burly cracks to a headwall. A fixed pin can be clipped or skipped, and a bolt anchor tops the pitch.

review.changed: Wrote both pitches with grades and lengths.

pitch_detail.notes: Careful face moves, with small fiddly placements, round the arete to a good ledge where the belay is built from gear.
Finger splitters to a blind move, more fingers, then a burly undercling to a gear belay on a small ledge.
Go left past the corner and jam a roof crack that is almost horizontal, then pull over its lip. Easy ground follows to a bolted anchor. Splitting the pitch in two gives the second a better belay.

review.changed: Wrote all three pitches. No lengths given.

pitch_detail.notes: Gear is hard to place among sand, soil and loose rock, but this lead gets you to the good pitches. Head for a small ledge a little right of and beneath the clear crack system.
From the ledge, follow the crack system, pull around a bulge (protect with large gear) and continue up a pleasant crack to a perch on the right.

Two hard sections, both needing large cams. Easier ground reaches a mass of stones wedged in the crack; a small roof is next, then jams and edges within the offwidth. The upper hard section is steep and strong. Bear left to the anchor as the crack ends.
Climb up the large gully to a chockstone and squeeze through it, leaving your pack. The anchors are just beyond.

review.changed: Wrote all four pitches with grades and lengths. No rappel table: only that you can rappel from all stations.

pitch_detail.notes: Bulges and slabs lead to a 4 m dihedral beneath a gully that slants left. Gear in the dihedral is good, and the exit into the gully is delicate. A solid anchor can be built partway up the gully.
Climb the gully to a chossy bulge, protected on the left, and surmount it with reasonable axe placements in sod (if frozen). Continue to the top with good gear.

review.changed: Wrote both pitches. No grades or lengths.
